issue.title: BufferGeometry
issue.body:
Hi!

I'm generating some pretty big models, and the creation of Vector3s, Face3s etc. is simply too slow. Even if I let a WebWorker to most of the job, the creation of the THREE-classes still has to happen in the main thread. @jeromeetienne pointed out that there's something called BufferGeometry, but we're having a hard time getting it to work.

I tried looking at the CTMLoader, but no success so far. Would it be possible to get a small introduction/example on how it works?

I have populated the buffers, but apparently, I can't just throw the BufferGeometry into a Mesh, as it complains about geometryGroups offsets.

Thanks,
Olav.

body:
I found the problem. CTMLoader computes offsets to make sure than no indices in the chunk are more than 65K apart. However, some large CTM encoded models may have triangles with such vertex indices. CTMLoader goes into infinite loop in this case.

Not sure how to fix it with the current BufferGeometry implementation. Perhaps the models should be optimized for chunking.
Maybe splitting the geometry in different objects instead?

Organic splitting is not easy in most cases. For instance, for 3D scans or photogrammetry models. It should be possible to come up with something based on bounding box, but it's not straightforward. 

Curiously enough, CTMLoader has code for rearranging vertexes, though it doesn't handle this situation. I'll take a look.

I have a fix. Had to modify CTLLoader to duplicate the vertices from sprawled faces. Seems to work nicely:

http://vizup.com/demo/webview-teapot-3.5M.html - huge model, 3.5 millon triangles, loads like a charm.

I'll test a bit more. If anyone interested in changes, ping me.
Yeah, would be nice to know what the actual fix is. A PR would be even better :)

Here is the fix - https://github.com/alboko/three.js/blob/master/examples/js/loaders/ctm/CTMLoader.js

I also updated ctm.js to the latest code (r12) from js-openctm.
Cherry picked into the `dev` branch. Thanks! :)

Unfortunately this fix is incomplete. The sprawled triangle fix from alboko will make the model load and render but will generate an insane amount of draw offsets in large and complex meshes with alot of vertex reuse.

I have provided an additional patch that adds the offset computation and buffer reordering method to BufferGeometry and changes the CTMLoader to use it instead of it's own brew.

The pull request is here:
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/pull/4433 

Hopefully this will close this one :)
